themes_detail.label: Food Poisoning Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Food poisoning complaints spiked 357% to 4 cases last week versus 0.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.0), signaling a potential foodborne illness outbreak or contamination event in East New York/Cypress Hills requiring urgent health department investigation.
evidence: 4 food poisoning complaints last week vs. 0.9 weekly baseline (357% increase, z-score: 4.0)
Spike represents highest statistical deviation in recent dataset
Temporal clustering suggests common source rather than random incidents
reporting_angles: Interview affected residents to identify common restaurants, food vendors, or suppliers; cross-reference with DOHMH inspection records
Investigate whether Health Department has issued violations or issued alerts to businesses in the district in past 2 weeks

themes_detail.label: Worship Venue Noise Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints from houses of worship surged 586% two weeks ago to 6 complaints versus 0.9 weekly average (z-score: 3.76), suggesting either new loud gatherings, enforcement gaps, or a specific problematic venue in the district.
evidence: 6 house of worship noise complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.9 weekly average (586% spike, z-score: 3.76)
Distinct from general noise category, suggesting concentrated problem at specific venue(s)
Spike is temporally isolated and recent
reporting_angles: Map 311 complaints geographically to identify which house of worship(s) generated complaints; interview neighbors and venue leadership
Examine whether community has standing zoning enforcement issues or if this represents new operations/events at existing venues

themes_detail.label: Vehicle Noise Escalation
themes_detail.summary: Vehicle noise complaints jumped 153% last week to 19 complaints versus 7.5 weekly average (z-score: 2.92), indicating a surge in loud vehicles, modified exhausts, or street racing activity that warrants NYPD coordination and enforcement review.
evidence: 19 vehicle noise complaints last week vs. 7.5 weekly baseline (153% increase, z-score: 2.92)
Subcategory spike isolated from broader noise trend, suggesting specific vehicle-related phenomenon
reporting_angles: Interview residents on which streets/times vehicle noise peaks; identify patterns (street racing, modified vehicles, commercial trucks)
Check NYPD data on 311-linked enforcement activity and noise summonses issued last week; assess whether precinct is responding to complaints

themes_detail.label: Broader Noise Trend (3-week lag)
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints generally elevated 3 weeks ago at 33 complaints versus 18.6 weekly average (77% increase, z-score: 2.94), though this trend has cooled since; warrants monitoring to determine if vehicle/worship spikes represent new escalation or echo of earlier surge.
evidence: 33 total noise complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 18.6 weekly average (77% spike, z-score: 2.94)
More recent vehicle and worship subcategory spikes suggest noise may be re-escalating after period of relative calm
Timing lag of 3 weeks reduces immediacy relative to current-week vehicle noise spike
reporting_angles: Determine whether the 3-week-old general noise spike and current vehicle/worship subcategory spikes represent related phenomena or separate incidents
Assess community board or local elected officials' recent enforcement requests on noise

themes_detail.label: Illegal Parking Decline
themes_detail.summary: Illegal parking complaints dropped 28% this week to 266 cases versus 367 weekly average (z-score: -2.45), representing the largest volume complaint category but trending downward—may signal improved enforcement, changed resident behavior, or data reporting lags rather than a story opportunity.
evidence: 266 illegal parking complaints this week vs. 367 weekly average (28% decline, z-score: -2.45)
Illegal parking remains highest-volume complaint category over 90 days (4,576 total) despite week-over-week drop
Downward trend is opposite of emerging problem signal
reporting_angles: Investigate whether NYPD parking enforcement has increased activity or if holiday/weather cycle explains drop
Monitor whether decline is sustained or temporary fluctuation
